what: The panel is divided into 16px cells (8px below panel width 768) and 100 colored cells are scattered across it. Each cell rests 10~100 frames, then on every frame has a 10% chance to roll one cell into an empty neighbor (up, down, left or right) over 10 frames with cubic-bezier(0,0,1,.4) — hesitant at first, then dropping into place at the end. Cells never overlap or leave the panel, and share the four colors (--fx-c1~c4) in turn. Steps are counted at 60fps so the tempo is the same regardless of screen speed

options.count: Number of cells, default 100 (no more than half the board’s cells)
options.chance: Chance of leaving on each frame after a rest, default .1
options.ease: Rolling curve, four Bézier values, default 0,0,1,.4
options.[data-fx-part=avoid]: Children (logo, title) left out when first scattering — the cells don’t start above them

note: Draws a 2D canvas at the very back of the page (z -1) — it sits under text and buttons and never blocks press or scroll. The original’s first screen is a flat grid seen from above, so 2D looks the same. The 3D cubes that roll over their edges in the tilted world after entering are in world.js of voxel-world-company-intro. With reduced motion, it stays parked at the first scattered positions.
